evidence.claim: The study observed four healthy volunteers at the second bilateral parasternal interspace during tidal breathing and static lung-volume conditions.
evidence.study_context: Healthy seated volunteers; 7.5-MHz transducer; 2–3 cm lateral to the sternum.
evidence.limitations: Very small trained convenience sample.

evidence.claim: During tidal inspiration the midpoint of the parasternal muscle moved ventrally and its borders straightened.
evidence.study_context: Tidal inspiration in four healthy seated participants.
evidence.limitations: Geometric motion is not equivalent to thickening or whole-muscle work.

evidence.claim: Parasternal thickness and inter-rib distance did not significantly change during tidal breathing.
evidence.study_context: Tidal breathing at the second parasternal interspace.
evidence.limitations: Does not test maximal effort or diaphragm dysfunction.

evidence.claim: The analysis used manual offline tracing and was sensitive to resolution, alignment, landmark identification, and sound-velocity assumptions.
evidence.study_context: Early ultrasound acquisition and offline digitization.
evidence.limitations: Limits precision and modern protocol transfer.

evidence.claim: The study assessed bilateral second and third parasternal muscles in 20 stable COPD patients using fixed B-mode settings and repeated images.
evidence.study_context: Cross-sectional exploratory COPD study with an experienced operator.
evidence.limitations: No healthy control group and limited sample.

evidence.claim: Thickness measurements showed high intra-rater and fair-to-excellent inter-rater reliability across fixed parasternal sites.
evidence.study_context: Repeated stored-image measurements in stable COPD.
evidence.limitations: Operators had respiratory-ultrasound experience; reliability was lower in obesity.

evidence.claim: Mean parasternal thickness correlated positively and echogenicity negatively with FEV1 percent predicted.
evidence.study_context: Twenty stable COPD patients; exploratory regression.
evidence.limitations: Association does not establish prognostic or causal validity.

evidence.claim: The negative association between parasternal ultrasound thickness and lateral CT intercostal mass was unexpected and may reflect site-dependent roles or a non-linear relationship.
evidence.study_context: Only 16 participants had usable CT correlation data.
evidence.limitations: Different chest-wall sites and small sample prevent interchangeability.

evidence.claim: Twelve healthy young men underwent right anterior, lateral, and posterior intercostal thickness measurements at rest and maximal inspiration.
evidence.study_context: Paired B-mode study; one examiner.
evidence.limitations: No women, diseased participants, or moderate effort conditions.

evidence.claim: Maximal inspiration increased thickness in anterior interspaces 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6, but not in the tested lateral or posterior interspaces.
evidence.value: anterior ICS 1,2,3,4,6 significant; lateral/posterior not significant
evidence.study_context: Resting expiration compared with maximal inspiratory breathing.
evidence.limitations: Multiple site comparisons in 12 participants; site and task specific.

evidence.claim: Intra-rater ICC at anterior interspaces 2–4 ranged from 0.649 to 0.836 across rest and maximal breathing.
evidence.study_context: Two measurements by the same examiner.
evidence.limitations: No inter-rater assessment.

evidence.claim: At lateral and posterior sites the internal and external intercostal layers overlapped and were not separable with the study's simple transverse imaging protocol.
evidence.study_context: Interpretation of null lateral/posterior thickness findings.
evidence.limitations: A null result may partly reflect measurement geometry.

evidence.claim: The investigation comprised 23 healthy subjects, 16 pressure-supported patients, and 54 patients assessed at first spontaneous breathing trial.
evidence.study_context: Three prospective physiological/diagnostic substudies.
evidence.limitations: Different substudies answer different questions and should not be pooled as one cohort.

evidence.claim: TFic was measured at the second right parasternal interspace 6–8 cm from the sternum using M-mode and the average of at least three breaths.
evidence.value: second right ICS; 6–8 cm; at least 3 breaths
evidence.study_context: Semi-recumbent participants and patients; 10–15 MHz linear probe.
evidence.limitations: One-sided fixed-site protocol.

evidence.claim: Parasternal thickening fraction decreased as pressure support increased.
evidence.study_context: Sixteen mechanically ventilated patients across randomized support conditions.
evidence.limitations: Physiological responsiveness does not validate a treatment threshold.

evidence.claim: TFic was higher with diaphragm dysfunction and inversely associated with diaphragm pressure-generating capacity.
evidence.study_context: Fifty-four mechanically ventilated patients; dysfunction defined by magnetic stimulation.
evidence.limitations: Association reflects compensatory recruitment, not a causal effect of measurement.

evidence.claim: TFic was higher during failed SBT and discriminated SBT failure in the derivation cohort.
evidence.study_context: Twenty-two SBT failures and 32 successes within one cohort.
evidence.limitations: No independent threshold validation and no proof that using TFic improves patient outcomes.

evidence.claim: The study obtained 236 bilateral inspiration/expiration measurements at one posterior rhomboid site in 59 healthy participants.
evidence.study_context: Healthy adults; prone position; three repetitions by one experienced examiner.
evidence.limitations: Repeated measurements are not independent participants.

evidence.claim: Posterior skin-to-pleura and rhomboid-to-pleura distances were smaller at maximal inspiration than expiration, while skin-to-rhomboid depth did not differ.
evidence.value: skin-pleura 23.1±5.4 vs 24.6±5.7 mm; rhomboid-pleura 9.5±2.6 vs 10.1±2.5 mm
evidence.study_context: Single posterior thoracic measurement point in healthy participants.
evidence.limitations: Cannot be transferred to parasternal or other procedural sites.

evidence.claim: BMI, sex, and thorax circumference explained 69.7 percent of variance in pleura depth within the fitted dataset.
evidence.study_context: Hierarchical regression on a healthy convenience sample.
evidence.limitations: No external validation; prediction error remains substantial.

evidence.claim: The authors limit the model to healthy subjects and one measurement point and call for larger normative and multi-site studies.
evidence.study_context: Scope of the dry-needling safety model.
evidence.limitations: No patient or external-site applicability.

evidence.claim: The editor states that the article was withdrawn after the data were found to be completely plagiarized from another researcher's work.
evidence.study_context: The Zotero attachment contains the retraction notice rather than the original article.
evidence.limitations: The stored abstract still exposes withdrawn numerical results and must not be used.

evidence.claim: The stored metadata reports a 15.38 percent threshold and diagnostic accuracy values from the withdrawn article.
evidence.study_context: Stale abstract metadata conflicts with the attached retraction notice.
evidence.limitations: Retracted result; ineligible for synthesis.

evidence.claim: The study measured width, skin-to-liver-capsule distance, stiffness, and liver visibility at four right lower intercostal sites during end inspiration and expiration in 59 liver patients.
evidence.study_context: Repeated-measures study for liver transient elastography probe placement.
evidence.limitations: Not designed to quantify parasternal muscle effort.

evidence.claim: End inspiration increased intercostal width and stiffness, while the respiratory effect on skin-to-liver-capsule distance was site dependent.
evidence.value: width respiration p<0.001; stiffness respiration p<0.001; SCD interaction p<0.001
evidence.study_context: Four 7th/8th anterior- and mid-axillary sites.
evidence.limitations: Anatomical window findings cannot be converted into ITF.

evidence.claim: Width and SCD measurements had ICC at least 0.97, and Site 3 was recommended for the study's liver elastography purpose.
evidence.study_context: Single-element transient-elastography probe placement.
evidence.limitations: Stiffness reliability was lower and the recommendation was not tested against histology across diverse populations.

evidence.claim: The sample was limited to 59 Chinese adults, intercostal size was measured in one dimension, and the findings require validation across populations and probe types.
evidence.study_context: Limits on generalizing the proposed measurement site.
evidence.limitations: No universal acoustic-window standard is established by one study.

evidence.claim: Thirty-eight healthy volunteers completed three exercise loads under five randomized ventilatory settings with oesophageal pressure, DTF, and ITF measurements.
evidence.study_context: Young healthy physiological NIV experiment with one trained sonographer.
evidence.limitations: No diseased or diaphragm-dysfunction group.

evidence.claim: ITF did not correlate with oesophageal pressure swing or DTF, whereas DTF correlated moderately with oesophageal pressure swing.
evidence.value: ITF-Poes rho=-0.040 p=0.361; ITF-DTF rho=-0.025 p=0.572; DTF-Poes rho=0.419 p<0.001
evidence.study_context: Healthy subjects across randomized NIV and exercise phases.
evidence.limitations: Negative finding applies to the tested healthy population and task range.

evidence.claim: ITF did not discriminate exercise loads in any ventilatory setup, while DTF and oesophageal pressure did.
evidence.study_context: Rest and Borg RPE 10/15 exercise loads.
evidence.limitations: Does not test maximal inspiratory manoeuvres or diaphragm dysfunction.

evidence.claim: The authors state that no direct clinical-practice conclusions should be drawn from the young healthy experimental sample.
evidence.study_context: Short standardized physiological experiment without follow-up.
evidence.limitations: Clinical NIV utility remains untested.

claims.text: The ultrasound-visible respiratory response of intercostal structures is site-, task-, and population-dependent rather than a universal thickening pattern.
claims.boundary: The seven eligible studies use different sites, respiratory tasks, and populations and cannot be quantitatively pooled.

claims.text: During quiet breathing, parasternal motion and straightening may occur without a measurable thickness change.
claims.boundary: Observed in only four healthy trained volunteers at the second parasternal interspace.

claims.text: Maximal inspiration produced measurable thickening mainly at anterior intercostal sites in healthy men.
claims.boundary: Twelve healthy men, one examiner, maximal task; lateral and posterior layers were not separable by the protocol.

claims.text: In healthy volunteers undergoing NIV, ITF did not track oesophageal pressure or distinguish the tested exercise loads.
claims.boundary: Thirty-eight young healthy participants; one sonographer; no diaphragm dysfunction or clinical respiratory failure.

claims.text: In mechanically ventilated patients, higher parasternal TFic was associated with lower support, diaphragm dysfunction, and failed SBT, consistent with compensatory recruitment.
claims.boundary: Prospective but small derivation substudies; SBT association is not an independently validated treatment rule.

claims.text: At fixed parasternal sites, thickness measurement was reproducible in stable COPD and showed modest associations with FEV1 percent predicted.
claims.boundary: Twenty patients, experienced operators, no controls; lower reliability in obesity and inconsistent relation to lateral CT muscle mass.

claims.text: Intercostal width, stiffness, and tissue depth vary with site and respiratory phase.
claims.boundary: The posterior dry-needling point and right inferior liver windows are different anatomical sites and their values are not interchangeable.

claims.text: At the studied posterior rhomboid point, the pleura was on average closer to the skin at maximal inspiration than expiration.
claims.boundary: Healthy participants, one posterior point, no external validation; not a universal safety distance.

claims.text: A universal intercostal thickening-fraction threshold can be used across healthy people, COPD, and mechanically ventilated patients.
claims.boundary: Populations, tasks, sites, and outcomes differ; the only additional threshold study in the corpus is retracted.

claims.text: The Ramaswamy 2023 diagnostic results are ineligible because the attached publication was retracted for complete data plagiarism.
The supplied corpus does not establish that using ITF or TFic to choose treatment improves patient outcomes.
A measurement protocol should fix anatomical site, body position, respiratory phase, probe orientation, ventilation setting, and breath averaging before values are compared.
claims.boundary: Methodological recommendation synthesized from heterogeneity in the supplied corpus, not a validated consensus guideline.
